report.tagline: A shopping app selling very cheap goods, mostly made in China, to shoppers in the US, UK, Europe and over 80 other countries.
report.simpleSummary: Temu is an app where you can buy a phone case for £2 or a dress for £8. Most items come straight from Chinese factories, which is why they are so cheap. The app feels like a game, with spinning wheels, coupons and countdown timers. It is owned by PDD Holdings, the company behind China's Pinduoduo.

overview.whatItDoes: Temu lets factories and sellers, mostly in China, sell directly to shoppers abroad at very low prices. Temu sets the selling price, runs the app and arranges shipping. Since the US ended duty-free entry for small parcels in 2025, Temu has moved more stock into local warehouses and onto local sellers.
howItWorks: Under the 'fully managed' model, a Chinese supplier sends stock to a Temu warehouse in China; Temu sets the retail price, markets it and ships it.
Under the newer 'local' or semi-managed model, sellers keep stock in US or European warehouses and ship themselves, which avoids per-parcel import duties.
Shoppers browse an endless feed of deals, collect coupons and play games such as spin-the-wheel for discounts.
Free shipping and free returns on the first return for most orders, plus price-adjustment refunds if the price drops.
Referral rewards give credits when friends sign up and buy.
overview.valueProposition: Very low prices on everyday items, gadgets and clothes, with free shipping and the fun of hunting for deals.

painPoints.howSolved: Factory-direct prices, often a third of high street prices.
Free shipping on most orders, with minimum order thresholds.
Games, flash deals and coupons make browsing feel like play.

painPoints.pain: Fear of losing money on a bad item.
painPoints.howSolved: Free first return within 90 days and credits for late deliveries.
Temu handles marketing, payments and shipping for them.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Temu controls pricing and logistics; suppliers just make and send goods.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps prices very low and consistent, and lets Temu move fast across countries.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Stock is held in the US or EU and shipped domestically.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Avoids per-parcel duties after de minimis rules ended, and speeds delivery.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Spin-the-wheel, Fishland, countdown timers and lightning deals.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Increases time in app and purchase frequency. Temu turned off spin-the-wheel in Europe in November 2026 under regulatory pressure.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Users get credits and free items for inviting friends.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Cheap growth channel that copies Pinduoduo's group-buying playbook.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Refunds the difference if the price drops; credit if delivery is late.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lowers fear of buying from an unknown seller.

steps.detail: Sees a 'Shop like a billionaire' style ad on Facebook or TikTok.
Gets a welcome coupon and a spin-the-wheel offer.
Scrolls an endless feed of £1 to £10 items.
Adds extra items to reach free shipping.
Pays by card, Apple Pay or PayPal.
Items arrive in 5 to 12 days from China, or 2 to 5 days if from a local warehouse.
App offers free items if three friends sign up.
Sends the link on WhatsApp or Snapchat.
Each friend gets their own welcome coupon.
Student gets credits or free products.
Uses the credit, adding more paid items to reach the threshold.
Selects the item in the app and picks a reason.
Picks credit to the Temu balance for a faster refund, or card.
Drops at a post office or courier point; first return free.
Either keeps buying cheap items or stops trusting the app.

businessModel.summary: Temu buys goods from suppliers at a very low price, sells them at a slightly higher price, and keeps the gap. With local sellers it takes a commission instead. It spent billions on ads to grow, and in 2026 cut marketing to focus on profit.

revenueStreams.detail: Temu pays the supplier a fixed price and sets the retail price; the difference is its revenue, reported as transaction services.
Sellers on the local warehouse programme pay a percentage of each sale.
Suppliers can be fined for delays or poor quality, though this is a small slice.

businessModel.pricing: Free to use. Items commonly priced from about £1 to £20 in the UK or $1 to $25 in the US. Free shipping on most orders. In the US, prices rose in 2025 after tariffs, and an import charge line appeared on some orders.
costDrivers: Marketing: huge spend on Meta, Google and TikTok ads, plus Super Bowl ads in 2023 and 2024
Import duties after the US and EU ended low-value parcel exemptions
Compliance costs and fines in Europe
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £20 UK order of five items, Temu might pay suppliers about £12 and spend £4 to £5 on air shipping and handling. That leaves about £3 to £4 before marketing. If a new customer cost £15 to £25 in ads to win, Temu loses money on the first order and only profits if the customer buys several more times. EU duties of €3 per item category from July 2026 can wipe out the margin on a €12 item, which is why Temu is pushing local warehouses.

howTheyGetUsers: Massive paid ads on social media and Google
Referral rewards and free gifts for inviting friends
Influencer haul videos on TikTok and YouTube
Launching in new countries every few months
whatBringsUsersBack: Push notifications about price drops and coupons
Credits in the Temu balance that must be spent
The sheer number of cheap items to discover
growth.moat: Temu's edge is cost: direct access to thousands of Chinese factories and PDD's deep pockets (over RMB 450 billion in cash). That is hard for Western retailers to match. But the moat is weaker than it looks, because tariffs and duties can erase the price gap overnight.

northStar.metric: Monthly repeat purchasers whose order arrived as described
northStar.why: Temu's model only works if customers come back without more paid ads. Counting repeat buyers who were happy with the item measures real value, not just installs from ad spend.

improvementIdeas.idea: Verified quality badge based on return rates and buyer photos, shown in search.
improvementIdeas.problem: Buyers cannot tell good items from junk, leading to returns and churn.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer returns and higher repeat purchase.

improvementIdeas.idea: Show 'arrives in 3 days from local warehouse' filter and rank local items first.
improvementIdeas.problem: Slow delivery from China and new duties per parcel.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Faster delivery, better margins after duties.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of orders from local warehouses

improvementIdeas.idea: Replace pressure games in all markets with a simple loyalty tier based on spending.
improvementIdeas.problem: Regulators and users dislike dark patterns; EU forced changes.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower regulatory risk and fewer uninstalls.

improvementIdeas.idea: Give refunds to the original card by default, with an opt-in bonus for credit.
improvementIdeas.problem: Users feel trapped when refunds become credit.

pmLessons: Growth bought with ads is fragile. When Temu cut marketing in 2026, revenue went flat. Look for organic repeat behaviour.
Regulation can change a business model overnight. The end of duty-free small parcels forced Temu to rebuild its logistics.
Games and urgency increase engagement but can cross into dark patterns that regulators ban.
Price is a strong hook, but quality and trust decide whether customers return.

interviewQuestions.question: The US removed duty-free entry for small parcels. How would you change Temu's product?
interviewQuestions.hint: Identify the cost impact per order. Options: local warehouses, bigger baskets, price changes. Pick one, show user and margin impact, and metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure if Temu's gamification is healthy or harmful?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare engagement with satisfaction and long-term retention. Track complaints, uninstalls and regulatory risk as guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: Temu cut marketing 17% and revenue went flat. What would you do as PM for retention?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why users stop buying: quality, delivery, price. Propose two features, prioritise by impact and effort, define success.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to build trust with first-time UK buyers.
interviewQuestions.hint: List fears: quality, delivery, refunds. Ideas: quality badges, delivery promise, easy refunds. Choose one and set metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Temu's and Shein's business models.
interviewQuestions.hint: Temu: everything store, fully managed, lowest price. Shein: fashion, test-and-reorder supply chain. Compare risks from tariffs and brand.

glossary.meaning: Gross merchandise volume: the total value of goods sold on a platform.
A rule letting low-value parcels enter a country without import duty; the US limit was $800 until 2025.
A setup where the platform, not the seller, sets the price and handles marketing and shipping.
Using game features like spins, points and timers to make people use an app more.
Design tricks that push users to do things they might not choose freely.
How much a company spends on marketing to win one new paying customer, also called CAC.
What a company keeps from one order after paying the direct costs of that order.
An EU law that makes large online platforms manage the risks of illegal and harmful content and products.
The single number a company uses to measure the value it delivers to users.
Numbers that must not get worse while a team pushes its main goal.
Something that makes a business hard for rivals to copy.

assumptions: Temu GMV and user numbers are outside estimates; PDD does not report Temu separately.
The £20 order unit economics uses rough estimates for supplier cost, shipping and acquisition cost.
The 'transaction services' line includes Temu revenue but may include other items.
